transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Aisha Khan (Latitude Channel Lead), Tom Rivera (Latitude VP Sales), Diego Alvarez (Latitude SE), Maya Patel (Latitude Legal)

Summary: quick pipeline review and alignment on who owns what, identify the top technical blockers for the Acme Retail POC, agree next steps for joint outreach.

[00:00] Sofia Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. I'll kick us off. Quick agenda — go over the joint pipeline, surface any blockers, confirm owners for demos and POCs, and agree next steps. Aisha, you good to start with a quick run of the top deals?

[00:18] Aisha Khan (Latitude): Yeah, sure. Thanks Sofia. We have — ok so top of the list is Acme Retail, they're our highest ARR potential. Champion there is Jenna Park in data platform. We're lined up for a discovery next Tuesday, they asked for a POC that shows improved recommendation latency and cost per inference. Second is Meridian Health, interest in private deployment for PHI. Third is Northbridge Financial, exploring embeddings for search. A bunch of smaller pipeline items too but those are the three we want to focus on for co-sell.

[01:02] Marcus Lee (Redwood SE): Quick clarifying Q — when you say "private deployment" for Meridian, do they explicitly want on-prem or VPC? Those are different asks and we'll need separate capacity/ops commitments.

[01:12] Aisha Khan (Latitude): Good call. They said "private control plane, VPC preferred", but they also asked about an on-prem option for a later phase. For now VPC.

[01:25] Tom Rivera (Latitude VP Sales): Also want to flag timing — Meridian says Q1 procurement cycle, but they need SOC 2 type 2 evidence and an audit log walkthrough.

[01:39] Priya Nair (Redwood CSM): We can provide SOC 2 artifacts and audit log screenshots, also have a compliance pack — I'll attach that to the follow-up.

[01:52] Diego Alvarez (Latitude SE): For Acme Retail's perf ask — what are your recommended models / setup and can Redwood run a baseline benchmark? We need numbers to compare to their existing endpoint which is on a managed endpoint.

[02:03] Marcus Lee (Redwood SE): Yes. For recommendation latency we usually recommend a quantized family for lower mem with batching and prefix caching. We'll suggest a model variant and run a short token-throughput benchmark. Need to confirm their sequence length and typical batch size. Diego, do you have that?

[02:18] Diego Alvarez (Latitude SE): Jenna indicated sequences around 256 tokens, batch sizes usually 8–16 during peak.

[02:25] Marcus Lee (Redwood SE): Perfect, that's in the sweet spot. We'll propose a Dedicated pool for the POC to ensure stable latency, but we can show comparative numbers for Hosted variants to highlight cost differences.

[02:40] Aisha Khan (Latitude): On pricing, do you have a recommended co-sell discount for deals where Latitude leads the intro? Our margin expectations are around 20% to make the motion viable.

[02:51] Sofia Chen (Redwood AE): We can do partner-tiered discounts for co-sell — I'll put numbers in the one-pager. For enterprise deals that go to Dedicated, there are commit thresholds. I'll include both hosted unit-pricing and dedicated commit guidance.

[03:06] Maya Patel (Latitude Legal): From a contracting perspective, we need to ensure the SLA and data residency language is clear. Also, mutual NDA — we reviewed your standard NDA but need small edits around indemnity. I'll send comments.

[03:19] Sofia Chen (Redwood AE): Thanks, Maya. We'll get legal aligned — Priya, can you coordinate on sharing the template and a basic SOW example?

[03:27] Priya Nair (Redwood CSM): Yep, will share the compliance pack, NDA, and SOW sample after call.

[03:36] Tom Rivera (Latitude VP Sales): Back to Acme — what's the typical timeline for a POC if Redwood runs benchmark and then a 2-week pilot? How long from discovery to pilot?

[03:46] Marcus Lee (Redwood SE): Discovery to pilot typically 2–4 weeks, depends on data access and infra approvals. If we get access to a representative dataset and some infra details, we can have a benchmark within a week and a pilot in 2 weeks.

[04:00] Aisha Khan (Latitude): Great. We'll try to lock Jenna for a discovery next Tue. Also, any concerns about integrations? They use an internal feature-store and Kafka streaming for inference calls.

[04:10] Marcus Lee (Redwood SE): Kafka is fine, we can front it with a small adaptor or use a lightweight queuing layer. Feature-store read latency matters; we'll want to get instrumentation on that. If feature-store adds 50–100 ms, that impacts end-to-end SLA.

[04:26] Diego Alvarez (Latitude SE): For Meridian Health, the PHI constraint — do you have a standard KMS integration for key management in VPC mode?

[04:34] Sofia Chen (Redwood AE): Yes, we support customer-managed KMS in private deployments and HSM options for on-prem later. We'll share the KMS integration docs.

[04:42] Marcus Lee (Redwood SE): Also note: if Meridian wants guaranteed PII isolation, Dedicated with strict tenancy is the safer path for the pilot. Hosted with VPC peering still has more shared control plane elements.

[04:57] Aisha Khan (Latitude): Ok makes sense. For co-selling, how do we handle OEM / product attribution? Some of our customers want Latitude branding on sales collateral.

[05:07] Sofia Chen (Redwood AE): Totally reasonable — we'll prepare a joint slide deck with a co-branding section. For legal terms, we can add a short clause in the SOW.

[05:17] Tom Rivera (Latitude): Competitors — a couple of deals asked about using Bedrock and Databricks. How should we position Redwood compared to those two?

[05:26] Marcus Lee (Redwood SE): Short answer: we lean on predictable latency and deployment flexibility. Bedrock is strong for model access but customers tell us performance and cost at scale is a common blocker; Databricks has strong data integration but not an inference-first optimized runtime. We'll share a short competitive comparison slide.

[05:42] Aisha Khan (Latitude): Nice. For the joint outreach — can we get a template email and a one-pager to send to prospects?

[05:49] Sofia Chen (Redwood AE): Yes — I'll send a one-pager and an outreach email template. Will include a call to action for an intro/demo and mention POC support.

[06:00] Diego Alvarez (Latitude SE): For the Acme POC technical deep-dive next week, who from Redwood should attend? I'd like both SE and someone who can talk about deployment (ops).

[06:08] Marcus Lee (Redwood SE): I'll lead the SE portion and bring our infra lead (Priya can loop in someone from our private deployments team if needed).

[06:17] Priya Nair (Redwood CSM): I'll invite Rajiv (private deployment lead) to the technical deep-dive.

[06:24] Maya Patel (Latitude Legal): And I'll follow up with our legal redlines — expect them by Friday.

[06:30] Sofia Chen (Redwood AE): Great. Let's capture owners: Sofia sends deck + pricing; Marcus preps benchmarks & tech checklist; Priya shares compliance pack and invites Rajiv; Aisha shares pipeline and champion contacts; Maya sends legal redlines.

[06:45] Tom Rivera (Latitude VP Sales): Quick ask — can Redwood provide an access matrix for roles (SSO / SAML / RBAC)? We need to show customer how we handle admin vs user access for audits.

[06:55] Priya Nair (Redwood CSM): Yes, we'll include the RBAC matrix in the compliance pack.

[07:03] Aisha Khan (Latitude): On outreach, let's prioritize Acme + Northbridge for joint emails; Meridian we'll treat as more sensitive due to PHI.

[07:13] Sofia Chen (Redwood AE): Agreed. We'll draft outreach for Acme + Northbridge first.

[07:20] Diego Alvarez (Latitude SE): One more technical note — Acme uses ~12k monthly inference QPS at peak for recommendations. That helps sizing.

[07:29] Marcus Lee (Redwood SE): Good to know. For 12k QPS we'll propose horizontal Dedicated scaling and show cost projection vs hosted.

[07:40] Sofia Chen (Redwood AE): Ok, last thing — timeline recap and next steps. We agreed: Sofia sends one-pager and pricing by 2026-12-02, Aisha shares pipeline list by 2026-12-04, Marcus preps benchmark checklist and schedule for Acme by 2026-12-04, schedule technical deep-dive week of 2026-12-07. Legal redlines from Maya by 2026-12-06.

[07:58] Maya Patel (Latitude Legal): Yep, I'll send redlines.

[08:03] Sofia Chen (Redwood AE): Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the doc pack and I'll create a shared folder for artifacts. Talk soon.

[08:12] Call ends.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker overlaps and some trade names mis-transcribed (e.g., Bedrock sometimes as "bed rock"). Occasional filler words and abbreviated sentences.
